A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SpodNet research. Their main text, equations, figures, and Appendices A–B are readable and support reliable matching despite figure revisions and pagination changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic precision-matrix recovery experiments, Animals graph-learning results, and training-stability and GLAD diagnostics in Appendix B.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and additionally reports GLAD's Animals result and empirical diagnostics of post-processing GLAD outputs.

M1.justification: The Schur-based updates, inverse maintenance, UBG/PNP/E2E architectures, training objective, and stabilization procedure are unchanged. The added explanation of the diagonal network's inputs does not change those inputs or its procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic sparse precision-matrix recovery across the same sparsity and sampling regimes and graph learning on Animals. The added GLAD diagnostics introduce no distinct dataset, population, or input-environment scenario.

E2.justification: Section 5.2 and Figure 6 add GLAD to the Animals comparison, which previously included GLasso and EGFM alongside UBG. The comparator set for synthetic recovery remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix B.3 adds two testing procedures: projecting GLAD-Z onto the PSD cone and masking GLAD-Theta using Z's support. The added Animals GLAD comparator is trained on the same data as UBG. Existing splits, metrics, and Appendix A settings are retained.

E4.justification: New Figure 9 tests whether simple post-processing remedies GLAD's constraint failures, examining sparsity and minimum eigenvalues after projection or thresholding. The existing normalization-instability and GLAD positive-definiteness-frequency analyses remain.

E5.justification: The existing shaded variability bands and statistical reporting practices are retained. v4 adds no repeated-run counts, seed information, uncertainty definitions, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: Figure 6 adds GLAD modularity of 0.72; UBG 0.78, GLasso 0.61, and EGFM 0.86 are unchanged. New Figure 9 shows projection reducing sparsity from 51.6% to 0% with minimum eigenvalue 0, and thresholded Theta having minimum eigenvalue -0.231. Figures 4–5 retain their result curves.

T1.justification: Propositions 3.1–3.2, their mathematical arguments, and the spectral-stability derivation are retained. The added parenthetical in Proposition 3.2's proof spells out block identities already present in the inversion formula.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal claims: a generic SPD-preserving architecture supporting additional structure, joint SPD/sparsity guarantees, and effective sparse precision estimation. Added experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v4 explains the rationale for the diagonal network's inputs and clarifies which off-diagonal constraints can be controlled. Appendix B.3 discusses why the tested GLAD repairs fail, while the conclusion adds computational cost and eigenvalue dynamics as unresolved research directions.

D1.justification: Sections 5 and 7 replace submission-only code and prospective-release statements with an explicit repository link for the PyTorch implementation. Appendix A's architecture descriptions and hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography and related-work discussion are unchanged. The positioning around joint SPD and sparsity guarantees is retained; the additional GLAD evaluations provide evidence for that existing position.

P1.justification: There are localized explanatory additions concerning block inversion, the GLasso objective, controllable constraints, and network inputs, plus revisions to the conclusion and code-access statements. Section order and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 4 moves its legend above enlarged panels, and Figure 5 is resized. Figure 6 is redrawn from three panels in one row to four panels in a 2-by-2 arrangement. Figure 9 is added, with accompanying figure relocations and page reflow.

improvement.justification: v4 strengthens the Animals evaluation by including a learned GLAD comparator and directly examines whether simple post-processing resolves GLAD's constraint failures in Figure 9. Clearer technical explanations and explicit code-access information also improve usability. These are useful, targeted gains while the core method, theoretical results, and existing benchmark findings remain stable.
